claim_boundary: Synthetic protocol interoperability gate only; not a coding benchmark or software-engineering capability score.

observed_evidence: Ten cases reached total_timeout. Deadline detection occurred a mean 14,148.4 ms and maximum 39,906.1 ms after the configured 60,000 ms deadline.

For timeout cases, the controller detected expiry a mean 1.58 ms after the in-flight provider call completed. This localizes nearly all pre-detection overshoot to non-cancelled provider calls begun before the deadline.
After detection, final controller test/diff collection plus cleanup and artifact writing took a mean 425.8 ms and maximum 456.1 ms.
Finalization itself averaged 363.6 ms; Docker cleanup after controller return averaged less than 66 ms in every timeout case.
cancellation_initiation_ms is null for every case because the current synchronous provider boundary exposes no cancellation mechanism.
deadline_diagnosis.proposed_future_change_not_implemented: Introduce an explicitly cancellable or deadline-aware provider-call boundary, pass the remaining controller budget into it, and separately cap final controller collection. Validate first on dedicated timeout fixtures and this frozen compatibility corpus; do not rerun or rewrite the preserved SWE-bench 0/2 result.

diagnosis.classification: Observed model/prompt-protocol incompatibility at tool initiation; provider adapter, parser, controller transition, and sandbox remained operational. The evidence does not fully separate base-model capability from sensitivity to RepoPilot's unchanged system prompt.
manual_hypotheses: The prompt requirement to emit PLAN text before editing may interact with this instruction-tuned model such that it continues narrating or simulating tool use instead of returning API function calls. This is a hypothesis requiring a future predeclared A/B compatibility study, not a change to this result.
A model trained more strongly for native function calling may pass the unchanged protocol. No alternative model was run because no other installed local model advertised tool capability.
observed_evidence: The endpoint advertised both completion and tools capabilities, and the same adapter/model passed a generic Responses function-call compatibility probe before the frozen SWE-bench pilot.
Across 45 model turns, the adapter produced 43 plan actions and 2 final actions, with zero function-call tool actions.
The text outputs explicitly named RepoPilot tools and often wrote pseudocode or fabricated tool outputs, showing awareness of the concepts without using the function-call channel.
All actions were syntactically parseable under the existing adapter: malformed-action rate, unknown-tool rate, and invalid-argument rate were all zero.
The controller consumed every plan action and advanced normally; 10 cases stopped only when the controller detected total_timeout, while 2 stopped on premature model_final.
No model-originated tool observation existed, so correction, sequencing, state-awareness, and recovery behavior could not be exercised.
All 144 sandbox security assertions, all 12 contamination gates, all 12 trace reconciliations, and all infrastructure checks passed.

known_limitations: Twelve synthetic cases measure protocol interoperability, not coding ability.
One repetition does not measure variance.
Prelude and fault evidence are deterministic fixtures, not naturally model-generated errors.

optional_second_model.reason: All five other already-installed local models advertised completion or completion-plus-vision but not tools capability. No model was downloaded and no unsuitable comparison was run.
